Frequently Asked Questions

What is a “dead bedroom”?

A “dead bedroom” is a relationship in which sex has become rare or has stopped altogether. Kristin Davin, writing for Choosing Therapy, calls it “an informal term and not a clinical diagnosis.”

What is considered a dead bedroom?

Davin gives two examples: a couple who have sex only on special occasions or holidays, and a couple who used to have sex several times a week and have gone several months without. The change from the couple’s own usual pattern is what counts; there is no official number.

He teaches intimate conversation for that talk, and he suggests a ritual for inviting sex and for saying no without any cost to the one who declines.

Is a dead bedroom the end of a marriage?

Not necessarily. In Gottman research, partners’ satisfaction with the sex, romance and passion in their marriage rests, by 70 percent, on the quality of their friendship. A “dead bedroom” may be a sign to tend the friendship first, and a couples therapist can help the two of you start the conversation.
